  • Wildcard enhances visibility for brands in AI-driven shopping environments.
  • 58% of U.S. shoppers now use AI to assist with purchases.
  • The startup supports new protocols for AI agent interactions in commerce.
  • Indian Americans are increasingly influential in shaping ecommerce technology.

YC Batch Year

Indian American entrepreneurs Kaushik and Yagnya have launched Wildcard, a Y Combinator-backed platform that is positioning itself at the forefront of AI-driven ecommerce discovery. The San Francisco-based startup, part of YC's Winter 2025 batch, aims to help online retailers win visibility across the rapidly expanding landscape of AI-powered shopping platforms.

Bridging Ecommerce and AI Search

Wildcard operates as an Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) platform built specifically for ecommerce and retail brands. As consumers increasingly turn to AI assistants like ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and Amazon Rufus to discover and purchase products, traditional search engine optimization is no longer enough.

"New applications are agentic and traffic to APIs will come from AI agents," the founders explained in their YC launch post. "Agents need interfaces that deliver outcomes, yet APIs are limited to discrete actions."

The platform tracks how brands, product categories, collections, and individual SKUs appear across AI search results. It then identifies visibility gaps and deploys AI agents to take corrective action — enriching product data, generating optimized content, creating comparison and collection pages, building FAQs, and improving discoverability across channels like Reddit, YouTube, and blogs.

The Agentic Commerce Frontier

What sets Wildcard apart is its bet on the emerging agentic commerce ecosystem. The company is building infrastructure to support new protocols like the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) and Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), which aim to standardize how AI agents interact with online stores and make purchases on behalf of consumers.

The startup also offers an open-source SDK and an agents.json registry that allows API providers to make their services discoverable to AI agents. According to the founders, developers can add their first integration in under 90 seconds, with 10 curated and officially verified APIs available at launch, including integrations with Resend and Alpaca.

Indian Americans Leading the AI Commerce Wave

Wildcard's launch adds to a growing roster of Indian American-founded companies shaping the future of commerce technology. The startup ecosystem in Silicon Valley continues to see strong representation from founders of Indian origin, particularly in AI and enterprise software.

With 58 percent of U.S. shoppers now reportedly using AI to assist with purchases, the timing of Wildcard's launch appears strategic. As AI shopping evolves from a novelty to a mainstream consumer behavior, platforms that help brands navigate this shift could prove essential.

The company is actively seeking partnerships with both API providers looking to prepare their services for AI agents and developers building agentic applications. As the ecommerce landscape undergoes its most significant transformation since the mobile revolution, Indian American entrepreneurs like Wildcard's founders are ensuring the diaspora remains at the cutting edge of innovation.
